title: I literally am so obsessed with @Signature Theatre production of Pipp...
transcript: Maybe this is a hot take, but my favourite Stephen Schwartz musical is Pippin. I have always loved this weird, messy, magical, existential crisis of a musical. And when I heard it was being performed in the round at Signature Theatre in Arlington, Virginia, I had to make the trip. And I'm so happy I did. Because somehow this musical that premiered on Broadway in 1972 and is set during the Holy Roman Empire, is more relevant than ever. If you don't know, Pippin is about a young prince who is trying to find his place in the world. He's looking for meaning and purpose in war, politics, power and sex. And the whole time he's being LED by this seductive theatrical form, that makes him feel chosen and special and destined for greatness, but might actually be guiding him towards his downfall. Can you see why this is so relevant for men in 2026? Anyway, this production is spectacular. I'm so happy. I love Pippin so much. Seeing him in the round, it's like how it's meant to be seen. Staging in the round adds such a level of intimacy. The temptation, the manipulation, the glitter. It's happening all around you. The cast is incredible. Bob Fosse directed this on Broadway and you can feel him in this piece. But the creative team of this production takes that DNA and makes it feel alive and modern. I just love the way the whole ensemble move and it's A little unhinged and a little strange, and is perfectly Pippin. Cedric Neil commands the room as a leading player. He is so magnetic and terrifying. And you understand why Pippin would follow him anywhere. And I adored Braden Bambino's Pippin. I believed every second of his journey. And his voice is insane. I cried through the entire last 20 minutes. What a specialty for Peter. Go see Pippin.
